doc.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025

title: Roland Kirk at The Fishnet
summary: He brought his big band to open for Roland Kirk at The Fishnet and was amazed by his multiple saxophones.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Yep. Roland Kirk. It was a jazz club, it was called The Fishnet. This guy just loved jazz. It only lasted a few years because not that many people were coming. And I brought the whole big band to play the opening of Roland Kirk in that place. And I’d never heard him play live, I mean I was like oy, yoy, yoy this is great oh my God and he’s playing all these saxophones you know. And the kids were going — because I said, “Well this is going to be a happening for you now,” I said, “you’ll probably never see this again.” So I said, “Pay attention. Watch and listen ‘cause this guy is unbelievable.” And I was the one going, “Oh my God, how’d he do that?” I mean he had all the saxophones set up and he’d play two notes with one finger on each saxophone. It must have been some just Rube Goldberg you know thing. I mean, but it was fun to listen to you know he had that manzello, that thing with the —
I saw him one time in Rochester and I think people were so stunned at the end of a piece he’d get this little bit of clapping and he says, “Thanks for that little pitter patter.”
